symbols.name: ground-set size
symbols.meaning: The size of the ground set $[h]$ whose three-element subsets index the banks.
symbols.quote: Fix the ground-set size $h=100$ and let $v=\binom h3=161700$ be the number of three-element subsets of $[h]$, and let $\mathcal T$ be the set of these subsets.

symbols.name: number of triples
symbols.meaning: The number of three-element subsets of $[h]$.
symbols.quote: Fix the ground-set size $h=100$ and let $v=\binom h3=161700$ be the number of three-element subsets of $[h]$, and let $\mathcal T$ be the set of these subsets.

symbols.name: bank size
symbols.meaning: The number of wires in each data bank.
symbols.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each data bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.

symbols.name: label-space dimension
symbols.meaning: The dimension of the label space used later.
symbols.quote: Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each data bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.

symbols.name: invocation count
symbols.quote: There are three stages, each running $v^2$ invocations with their own scratch wires, so $I=3v^2=78440670000$ is the number of invocations.

symbols.name: bit neighbour count
symbols.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the bit construction.
symbols.quote: A fixed triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}{2}=13968$ neighbours in the bit construction: three choices of the shared element, then two of the other 97 elements

symbols.name: complex neighbour count
symbols.meaning: The number of neighbours of a fixed triple in the complex construction.
symbols.quote: It has $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}{3}+3\cdot97=147731$ neighbours in the complex construction, intersection zero plus intersection two.

symbols.name: bit central wires
symbols.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the bit network.
symbols.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

symbols.name: complex central wires
symbols.meaning: The number of central wires per invocation in the complex network.
symbols.quote: There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.

symbols.name: bit wire count
symbols.meaning: The total number of wires in the bit network.
symbols.quote: The bit network has $W_{\rm b}=2N+I(vz_{\rm b}+c_{\rm b})=177176569091445000000$ wires

symbols.name: complex wire count
symbols.meaning: The total number of wires in the complex network.
symbols.quote: The complex network has $W_{\rm c}=2N+I(vz_{\rm c}+c_{\rm c})=1873807244643542670000$ wires; all these numbers are fixed, independent of the input length.

derivations.quote: Fix the ground-set size $h=100$ and let $v=\binom h3=161700$ be the number of three-element subsets of $[h]$, and let $\mathcal T$ be the set of these subsets.
Set $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ for the size of each data bank, and $m=h^3=1000000$ for the dimension of the label space used later.
There are three stages, each running $v^2$ invocations with their own scratch wires, so $I=3v^2=78440670000$ is the number of invocations.
In the bit construction, scalars lie in $\mathbb F_2$ and two triples $S,S'$ are neighbours when $|S\cap S'|=1$.
In the complex construction, scalars lie in $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$ and the neighbours of a triple are the distinct triples with even intersection (zero or two).
So for arbitrary initial scratch values, one forward invocation changes $y_S$ to $y_S+x_S$ and leaves every other value unchanged
A forward invocation $X\to Y$ at stage 1, the inverse schedule $Y\to X$ (which effects $X\gets X-Y$) at stage 2, and a forward invocation $X\to Y$ at stage 3 give
A fixed triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}{2}=13968$ neighbours in the bit construction: three choices of the shared element, then two of the other 97 elements
It has $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}{3}+3\cdot97=147731$ neighbours in the complex construction, intersection zero plus intersection two.
There are $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires per invocation in the bit network and $c_{\rm c}=101$ in the complex one.
The bit network has $W_{\rm b}=2N+I(vz_{\rm b}+c_{\rm b})=177176569091445000000$ wires
The complex network has $W_{\rm c}=2N+I(vz_{\rm c}+c_{\rm c})=1873807244643542670000$ wires; all these numbers are fixed, independent of the input length.
